mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 7% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: When CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) increases and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is high, it may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases and FEDFUNDS is above 4%
regime_hint: high inflation and high interest rates
failure_condition: If both CPI increases and FEDFUNDS are high but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong supply activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real federal funds rate (RSAFS) below zero indicates weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS is below zero but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% indicates monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% but S&P 500 returns are negative.
